correctness.rationale: For vertex character a each tree contributes the product of edge weights s_us_v with s_v=(−1)^a_v, including every tree even if several have the same parity mask. The signed matrix-tree formula therefore yields the stated cyclic minor. Global sign reversal preserves each edge weight, and cyclic and reflection symmetries of the rim preserve the minor; the thirteen orbits account for all 64 choices after fixing the hub sign. Independent exhaustive enumeration of all 924 six-edge sets found exactly 320 trees and returned spectrum {−52:12,−16:12,−4:40,0:38,12:12,16:12,320:2}, giving rank 90, nullity 38, least nonzero absolute value 4, Hilbert condition number 80 on the visible space and pseudoinverse norm 1/4. The inverse Walsh transform of the visibility indicator is the unique translation-invariant projection, with denominator 128 and replayed numerator counts {−38:1,−6:18,0:64,2:32,10:12,90:1}. Absolute column and row sums both equal 420/128=105/32, attained by a coordinate delta in ℓ¹ and aligned signs for a row in ℓ∞. Averaging conjugates of any projection over translations preserves its action as identity on the range and keeps its image in that range. The averaged map is necessarily Walsh diagonal and is the canonical projection; convexity proves its minimality over real and complex projections.

value.rationale: Degree parity is a natural coarsening of tree incidence, not an arbitrary choice of Fourier signs. Rim length six is the first noncomplete simple wheel in the period-three singular regime of the full edge model, making it a natural small case in which to ask whether the degree-parity observation retains singularity and what its recoverable range costs at endpoints. Rank and gap alone cannot answer the endpoint question. The whole parity spectrum and exact optimal constant 105/32 determine recoverability and the least possible endpoint projection amplification for this object, providing an independently usable exact benchmark without claiming a new general formula.
residual_risks: The result is finite and the particular constant is not asserted for larger wheel sizes or for the edge-incidence observable.
